title: Multistate Torsion in Zitterbewegung
abstract: We derive nonlinear Zitterbewegung velocity of electrons augmented by band torsion in crystals. The equation of motion with multistate quantum geometric tensors and torsion culminates in transient nonlinear photocurrent responses distinct from the recently measured resonant steady-state photovoltaic effects induced by circularly polarized light. Tomography protocols for measuring the multistate quantum geometric torsion tensors are proposed.
summary: This theoretical work develops a framework to analyze the nonlinear Zitterbewegung of electrons in crystals, incorporating the effects of band torsion using multi-state quantum geometric tensors. The key finding is that the resulting transient photocurrents offer a novel, direct method to measure the band torsion, bypassing limitations found in traditional resonant optical measurements.
main_problem: The paper derives and proposes methods to measure nonlinear Zitterbewegung velocity and associated transient photocurrent responses that are augmented by band torsion in crystals.
main_result: The nonlinear Zitterbewegung currents provide a direct, off-resonant diagnostic tool to access individual components of the quantum geometric multistate band torsion tensor, which is inaccessible via standard resonant measurements.
method: The analysis involves solving the quantum Liouville equation perturbatively to calculate higher-order density matrix elements, leading to the derivation of second-order Zitterbewegung velocities.
model_or_system: The system models electrons in clean crystals, utilizing a multi-state quantum geometric framework incorporating band torsion and higher-order quantum geometric tensors (QGTs).
key_observables: Multistate band torsion ($T_{nmp}^{ijk}$), nonlinear Zitterbewegung velocity ($\xi_m^{(2)}$), and transient nonlinear photocurrents ($j^{(2)}_i(t)$).
important_parameters: Second order in optical electric fields, clean crystal limit ($	au 	o \infty$), and specific polarization states (circular/linear).
main_assumptions: The analysis is based on semiclassical equations of motion for electron velocity and assumes the ultraclean system limit.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by deriving the equation of motion for electron velocity, extending the analysis to second order in optical fields, and finally relating the resulting transient photocurrents to the band torsion tensor via tomography protocols.
why_interesting: The connection between high-order nonlinear optical responses (like transient photocurrents) and fundamental geometric properties of the band structure (like band torsion) provides a powerful, non-perturbative diagnostic tool for quantum materials.
